intended_object: The n-Selmer group A(S,n) ⊆ Aˣ/(Aˣ)ⁿ of a finite étale algebra A ≅ ∏ Lᵢ over a global field. It is the set of classes whose component in each field factor Lᵢ lies in the S-Selmer group Lᵢ(Sᵢ,n), meaning it is unramified (has valuation divisible by n) outside Sᵢ. Here it is obtained by transporting along a given decomposition. This reading comes from the docstring, the module doc and the use in `selmerGroupA` for elliptic-curve descent.
explanation:
The definition pulls the product subgroup `selmerGroupPi` (the subgroup `Subgroup.pi` of the factor Selmer groups `selmerGroup (R := B i) (K := L i) (S := S i) n`) back along the isomorphism e : Aˣ/(Aˣ)ⁿ ≃* ∏ (Lᵢˣ/(Lᵢˣ)ⁿ). When e is induced by a ring decomposition A ≅ ∏ Lᵢ, this is exactly the standard Selmer group of the étale algebra: a class lies in it iff each component lies in the Selmer group of its factor. The lemma `mem_selmerGroupOfEquiv_iff` states exactly this.

The only odd feature is that e is any multiplicative isomorphism of the quotient groups, not necessarily one coming from a ring decomposition. For an unrelated e (for example an automorphism of ℚˣ/(ℚˣ)² swapping the classes of 2 and −1), the pullback is not the intrinsic Selmer group of A. But the docstring and module notes say plainly that the object is "transported along" a supplied decomposition, and that taking e as an input is deliberate because Mathlib cannot yet split étale algebras. The one use site in the library (`selmerGroupA`) supplies the real decomposition `AdjoinRoot.modPowEquivPiFactors`. So this is a caller precondition, not a wrong definition.

The generality is fine: the factors are arbitrary Dedekind domains with fraction fields, the index type is arbitrary, n is any natural number, and the sets Sᵢ are arbitrary. Mathlib has `IsDedekindDomain.selmerGroup` only for a single fraction field and has no Selmer group for products or étale algebras, so there is no counterpart.
